key_drivers: Three consecutive post-earnings declines despite six straight double beats: -5.64% (2 Jun 2026), -6.82% (17 Feb 2026), -7.42% (19 Nov 2025). The beat is not the trade here; the guide is

First full quarter consolidating CyberArk ($25bn, closed 11 Feb 2026) plus Chronosphere - consensus +32% YoY revenue is largely bought growth, and the organic/inorganic split is exactly where a messy print goes wrong
Forward P/E above 85x and P/S above 15x on a stock that made a 3-month high of $396 on 13 Aug; at $359 it is only 9% off that, so the de-rating into the print is partial
Options price a 10.5% move against a realised history of 5.6-7.4%, so the straddle is rich even if my direction is wrong
Management raised FY26 guidance after Q3 ($3.77-3.79 EPS, $11.42-11.43bn revenue), which removes the usual sandbag
what_would_change_my_mind: An FY27 initial guide with NGS ARR and RPO growth above the 59-60% / 32-33% bogey and a clean organic revenue number that shows the platformisation story is not just CyberArk arithmetic.
reasoning: The single most repeatable fact about this stock is that it beats and then falls. Three quarters running, each time by 5-7%, each time on guidance rather than the quarter. Nothing about this setup breaks that pattern: the multiple is higher, the FY26 guide was already raised so there is no sandbag left, and the first full CyberArk quarter gives the market a reason to discount the headline +32% as bought rather than earned. Against that, the stock is already 9% off its 13 Aug high and fell 5.9% today, and a 10.5% implied move is well above anything PANW has actually delivered - which is why this is Lean and not Strong. I expect a move smaller than the straddle, and more likely down than up.

key_drivers: Two large, well-known forces pointing opposite ways: $51.3bn AI server backlog and FY27 AI server guidance raised to ~$60bn from $50bn, against DRAM prices TrendForce sees up 13-18% QoQ into Q3
Consensus $45.1bn revenue / $4.91 non-GAAP EPS versus company guidance of $44-45bn, so the bar sits at the top of the guide
Q1 FY27 already printed +88% revenue growth and $16.1bn of AI-optimised servers (+757% YoY); the comparison base is now brutal
Options imply 11.4% into 4 Sep expiry - the market has no more idea than I do which force wins
Stock -5.3% today to $431.78, well off the $472 high of 27 Aug, so some of the risk has already come out
what_would_change_my_mind: A gross-margin line that shows Dell passing memory inflation through rather than absorbing it would make this a clear long; an AI backlog that fails to grow sequentially would make it a clear short.
reasoning: This is the cleanest abstention on the board. The revenue story and the margin story are both large, both well documented, and both fully in the public domain - which means the print is a referendum on which one the market chooses to weight, not on any information I can find. The margin risk is concrete and quantified (DRAM up 13-18% QoQ) but it is also the single most written-about thing about Dell this month, so it is not an edge. Meanwhile the backlog is genuinely enormous and the FY27 AI guide was already raised by $10bn. When both sides of a trade are this well lit, the honest answer is no call. I am confident only about size: an 11.4% straddle on a name that has repeatedly moved double digits deserves a high magnitude number.

key_drivers: The stock has already de-rated 25% into the print: $282.82 on 17 Aug to $211.68 now, and -30% from the 3-month high of $302.52. The 'priced for perfection' objection has largely been answered by the tape
Beat the consensus in each of the trailing four quarters with an average surprise of 27.4%; fiscal Q2 FY26 rallied over 15% on the print
Guidance $465-475m against consensus $470.7m (+111% YoY) and EPS $1.17 - Credo has consistently guided to a beatable number
The swing factor is the >$600m optical revenue projection and the promised second-half acceleration, not the quarter itself
TD Cowen raised its target to $300 from $260 on 18 Aug, so sell-side conviction survived the drawdown
what_would_change_my_mind: Any softening of the second-half optical ramp, or a customer-concentration disclosure showing a hyperscaler pulling in rather than adding - that turns a 25% pullback into the start of a de-rating rather than the end of one.
reasoning: Four straight beats averaging 27% surprise, into a stock that has just given back a quarter of its value in two weeks. That combination is what I am paying for. The bear case on Credo has always been the multiple, and 25% of the multiple has already gone; what is left is a company guiding to +111% revenue growth in a demand environment that has not deteriorated. The counterweight is that today's 6.5% fall is part of a market-wide AI-infrastructure selloff, and if that continues the reaction gets swamped by beta rather than driven by the print - which is why certainty is Low despite a clear lean. Magnitude is the confident part: this name moves 12-15% on prints routinely.

key_drivers: Last print (Q1 FY27, 28 May 2026) took the stock up 22.1% in a session on a 3.5% revenue beat, an 11.5% EPS beat and a raised full-year guide - the expectations bar was violently reset
The stock has held that repricing: $437.90 now against ~$402 immediately post-print, so none of the gain has been given back
Fundamentals are genuinely strong - Atlas +29.4% YoY for a fourth straight quarter above 29%, RPO +88%, cRPO +69% - which is exactly why they are priced
Consensus $1.62 EPS. MongoDB's guidance is habitually conservative, so a headline beat is close to the base case and tells you little about the reaction
A 4-6% pullback followed last quarter's pop despite near-universal target raises, so even the good outcome faded
what_would_change_my_mind: A full-year guide that raises the Atlas growth outlook again rather than merely reaffirming it would break the symmetry upward; Atlas decelerating below 29% would break it downward.
reasoning: A 22% single-session repricing three months ago is the whole story, and it cuts both ways. It proves the demand inflection is real, and it means the market now requires that inflection to continue merely to justify today's price. The stock never gave the gain back, so there is no discount to buy and no obvious excess to sell. Everything I can find about the business is good and everything I can find about the business is known. I decline the direction. On size I am confident: this is one of the most reliably explosive earnings names in software, it printed 22% last time, and 11% is if anything a conservative honest estimate.

company: Brown-Forman Corporation (calendar symbol BF.B; BF-B is the quote symbol that resolves - BF.B returns an empty chart)
key_drivers: FY27 guidance already resets the bar low: roughly flat organic net sales and organic operating income down 3-5%, reaffirmed after what the company itself called a turbulent first half
The stock is at $26.46, down from $28.75 on 24 Aug and grinding steadily lower - sentiment is on the floor, which cuts both ways
Fiscal Q1 is a seasonally small quarter for Brown-Forman, so it rarely carries enough news to reset the full-year view either way
Sector-wide negative revision cycle in spirits has repeatedly cleared low bars downward, but that dynamic is now thoroughly consensus
Unsuccessful deal talks referenced in the FY26 wrap remove a takeout floor that some holders had been leaning on
what_would_change_my_mind: Any change to the FY27 organic operating income range - a cut would confirm the sector pattern and a raise would be a genuine surprise; a reaffirmation tells me nothing.
reasoning: A beaten-down staple with guidance already cut to flat sales and declining operating income is the definition of a two-sided setup: the bar is low enough that a reaffirmation could pop it, and the sector's revision cycle is bad enough that even low bars keep getting missed. Both of those observations are widely held. Fiscal Q1 is also Brown-Forman's least informative quarter. I can construct the bull case and the bear case with equal ease from the same facts, which is the signal to abstain. Magnitude is the more answerable question and it is modest by this cohort's standards - a large-cap staple, not an AI name.

key_drivers: The stock closed at $46.54 on 31 Aug - its 3-month high - after running from a $25.83 low, so it enters the print at the top of its range with a 75%+ rally behind it
Persistent pattern of post-earnings selling: -12% premarket on 12 May 2026, -9% on a guidance update, -10.4% YTD despite repeated EPS beats
Q1 FY27 beat EPS by 53% and the stock still fell, because the FY27 guide implied 15-17% growth against 26% delivered in FY26 and EPS of $0.76-0.80 against $1.03 consensus
Q2 guidance is $272-274m and consensus sits at $273.1m - dead centre of the guide, leaving no cushion in either direction on the quarter itself
The Duo Agent Platform traction that drove the August rally is a narrative that has to be validated with bookings numbers this print, not merely referenced
what_would_change_my_mind: A raised FY27 revenue guide with Duo Agent attached to a disclosed ARR or bookings figure - that would turn the deceleration story into a re-acceleration story and the rally would be justified rather than borrowed.
reasoning: GitLab keeps beating the quarter and keeps falling, because the argument is about the growth rate and the growth rate keeps stepping down - 26% in FY26 to a guided 15-17% in FY27. The stock has just rallied more than 75% off its low and set a 3-month high yesterday on Duo Agent enthusiasm, which means it now needs the re-acceleration to be visible in the numbers rather than promised on the call. Q2 consensus sits exactly on the midpoint of company guidance, so the quarter itself cannot rescue it. This is the same setup that produced a 12% premarket drop in May, with a higher starting price. The clearest lean on the board after PANW.

key_drivers: FY26 guidance of 2% comparable store sales growth, with Q2 comps expected to look like Q1 - a deliberately unexciting bar
Trade-down demand from a value-conscious consumer is a genuine tailwind, and tariff-driven inventory dislocation improves closeout supply
The offsetting risk named in every preview is the same one: weaker traffic and margin pressure if closeout supply tightens instead
Stock at $71.57, -5.1% today and down from $76.35 on 24 Aug, so it enters soft rather than extended
Nothing in the public record differentiates this quarter from the last several for a steady-executing discount retailer
what_would_change_my_mind: A comp materially above the 2% run rate with gross margin held flat would be a genuine beat; a comp at 2% with margin compression from closeout sourcing would be the bear case confirmed.
reasoning: I could not find anything about this print that a competent reader of the guidance would not already know. Ollie's guided to 2% comps, the consumer backdrop supports the model, the closeout supply risk is the standing offset, and the company executes steadily. That is a description, not an edge. The one thing I would note is that the stock comes in soft rather than extended, which mildly reduces downside asymmetry, but not enough to move me off Neutral. Size is the answerable part: a mid-cap retailer with a comp-driven print typically moves mid-to-high single digits.

key_drivers: Consensus revenue of $214.4m sits below the $219.5m Sprinklr printed in Q1 FY27, so the street already models a sequential decline - the bar is genuinely low
Growth has decelerated to 7% total / 6% subscription YoY, which is the level at which small-cap software gets valued on cash rather than growth
Company Q2 EPS guidance of $0.10 and consensus of $0.104 leave essentially no gap on the quarter itself
At $7.84 and a $1.9bn market cap this is the smallest and least liquid name in the cohort, so the reaction is as likely to be positioning-driven as fundamentals-driven
Stock is up from $7.20 in mid-August but fell 4.5% today, so it is neither extended nor washed out
what_would_change_my_mind: Subscription revenue re-accelerating above the 6% run rate, or a buyback/strategic announcement alongside the print - at this valuation the capital-allocation news would matter more than the quarter.
reasoning: A decelerating small-cap SaaS name where the street has already marked revenue down sequentially is not a setup with an obvious side. The low bar argues up; the 7% growth rate and the absence of any visible catalyst argue that even a beat gets sold. The mild negative tilt in my direction score reflects the growth trajectory rather than anything about this quarter. Evidence quality is the weakest on the board - coverage is thin, most of what I found was calendar notices rather than analysis, and I could not source an implied move. That thinness is itself a reason to abstain rather than to guess.
